result.reasoning:
The headline claim survives and I reproduced it against real run data, but the reported failure scenario is wrong in its specifics and one of the two code paths it names is numerically a non-event.

CONFIRMED — mutate_window / mutate_constant bypass the steer arm's guidance, and nothing downstream re-checks it.
generator.py:234 and :246 end with `return child if is_valid_root(child) else None`; neither mentions `self.acceptable`. gp.py:656-668 `_mutate` dispatches "window"/"constant" straight to them, and gp.py:689 `_next_generation` only guards `if not is_valid_root(child)`. So a window/constant mutant enters the population and is paid for without ever meeting ban / MUST / first_form / thinning. The other four breeding paths (mutate_subtree, mutate_operator, mutate_hoist, crossover) and generate() all do call `self.acceptable`, so the hook installed at scripts/idea_search.py:208 is applied unevenly, exactly as reported.

The leak is visible in committed run data. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold/evidence.json has MUST = {day_distinct_ratio, day_es_ratio_hi, day_es_ratio_lo, day_gini, day_std, day_wstd}, and the steer archive contains three rows with no MUST operator at all:
  abs_(cs_demean(day_mean(in_stddev_rolling(in_slice(Ret, 2, 237), 5))))   <- seed #2, exempt via seeds_repr
  abs_(cs_demean(day_mean(in_stddev_rolling(in_slice(Ret, 2, 237), 15))))  <- NOT exempt
  abs_(cs_demean(day_mean(in_stddev_rolling(in_slice(Ret, 2, 237), 30))))  <- NOT exempt
The latter two are window mutants of seed #2 and the steer `acceptable()` refuses both with bucket ['outside']. I ruled out every other origin: the in_stddev_rolling node has shape.width = 236, so mutate_subtree skips it (generator.py:165); mutate_operator requires `s.name != node.spec.name` so it cannot keep in_stddev_rolling while only moving the window; mutate_subtree / mutate_operator / mutate_hoist / crossover all end in `if self.acceptable(child)` and would have returned the same 'outside' refusal. mutate_window(seed#2) produces the `...30)` row 315/2000 times. So these two trees were scored and archived while the guidance would have refused them, and they are not in the 430 `proposed`.

mutate_constant leaks differently and also reproduces: on `mul(cross_ema(day_gini(Ret), 30), 3)` it returns `mul(..., -0.5)`, `mul(..., -1)`, `mul(..., 1)` etc., every one of which has dedup_key `cross_ema(day_gini(Ret),30)` (C6_shift_scale_const rewrites a root add/sub/mul-by-constant to its operand), so the steer `acceptable()` refuses each as ['equivalent']. Unbounded canonical-duplicate re-spellings can breed through this path — which is the exact budget waste first_form was added to stop.

REFUTED sub-claim 1 — the stated failure scenario cannot happen. `cross_ema.windows = (3, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 241)`: 1 is not in the pool, so mutate_window can never emit `cross_ema(day_gini(Ret), 1)`. And C1_window1_identity's pattern is `{ts_min|ts_max|ts_mean|ts_med|ts_sum|ts_decay_linear}(_, 1)` — cross_ema is absent, so `dedup_key("cross_ema(day_gini(Ret), 1)")` stays `cross_ema(day_gini(Ret),1)` and first_form would not call it equivalent. The real run's counters agree: equivalent = 0, banned = 0. The mechanism that actually fires for mutate_window is the MUST / `outside` gate (243 of 430 rejections in that run), not the window-1 identity rewrite. Related: ban rules are window/constant-insensitive by construction ($w matches any number — verified banned() unchanged for ts_product(...,30) vs (...,60) and cross_zscore(...,30) vs (...,60)), and MUST is a name-set test on the expression string, so a window or constant change can never flip ban, and can only flip MUST for a tree that was already outside it (a seed, as here).

REFUTED sub-claim 2 — the generate() `_collapse_leaf` fallback is real in code but cannot move a number. I instrumented `_root_ops_of`, which generator.py calls on one line only (:125, the fallback): 0 fallbacks in 4000 generate() calls under the real steer `acceptable`. Per-proposal acceptance is 34.6% (2.89 acceptable()-checks per generate()), so P(64 straight rejections) ~= 1.6e-12 against a per-arm budget of 192 trees. The reporter's three `day_quantile_q75(Vwap)` / `day_last(Open)` / `day_pos_ratio(Amt)` trees only appear because they forced `acceptable` to always-False, a state that never occurs. Note also that `_collapse_leaf` is reached from `_gen` (:305) during ordinary construction, so counting `_collapse_leaf` calls — as the suggested fix implicitly does — overstates the fallback by ~250x.

REFUTED sub-claim 3 — the arm comparison itself is not corrupted. `scored` (123 steer / 170 control), `live`, `passers` come from the scorer instances and the archive CSV, not from `stats`, so they count every tree actually paid for, mutants included. Only the `sampling` diagnostic is undercounted. Impact on the e1_I2 verdict is small: 2 of 102 archived steer rows (~2%), both scoring -0.90 and -1.04, so "0 passers" does not flip. Severity medium is fair for the correctness hole, not for that episode's conclusion.

result.corrected_fix:
Close the hole in install() (scripts/idea_search.py, inside the same closure that already patches _pick/acceptable), but only for the two mutators, and fix the counter semantics at the same time.

1. Wrap only mutate_window and mutate_constant. Capture `_mw, _mc = T.mutate_window, T.mutate_constant` next to `_acceptable, _pick`, and inside install() add:

    def guarded(fn):
        def wrapped(self, expr):
            child = fn(self, expr)
            if child is None:
                return None
            return child if self.acceptable(child) else None
        return wrapped
    T.mutate_window, T.mutate_constant = guarded(_mw), guarded(_mc)

   and restore them in the same place the script already restores `T._pick, T.acceptable` after each arm. Returning None is safe and is the right degradation: gp.py:657-668 `_mutate` shuffles all five kinds and falls through to `self.generator.generate()`, which does honour the patched acceptable, and gp.py:689 still guards is_valid_root. For the control arm `acceptable` is the unpatched one, so the wrap is a no-op there and the arms stay comparable.

2. Do NOT wrap generate() and do NOT add the suggested _collapse_leaf fallback handling. It fires 0 times in 4000 calls (P ~= 1.6e-12 per call), and the proposed behaviour — "return the last legal tree" — is not implementable as described: generate()'s loop at generator.py:117-124 discards each rejected tree and keeps no reference, so there is no last legal tree to return. If a belt-and-braces guard is still wanted, the only correct form is to re-call generate() a bounded number of times and, if still unacceptable, raise or return the collapse-leaf tree while recording stats["fallback"] — but it should be understood as dead code, not as a fix that changes any number.

3. Fix what the counter means, or the fix will look like it made things worse. `stats["proposed"]` counts guidance DECISIONS, not trees evaluated: mutate_subtree and mutate_operator call acceptable up to max_retries (16) times per successful mutation, so proposed already over-counts distinct trees while under-counting evaluated ones. After the wrap, proposed will rise and still not equal `scored`. Either rename it, or add an explicit distinct-tree counter — e.g. `stats["decisions"]` for every acceptable() call and a `seen_keys` set whose size is the number of distinct trees that passed — and write both into evidence["arms"][arm]["sampling"] so the diagnostic can be read against `scored`.

4. While there: the seed exemption at the top of acceptable() tests `e in seeds_repr` on the canonicalised parsed seed, so a seed's own window/constant mutants are correctly NOT exempt. That is exactly why the wrap makes MUST bite on the two archived `in_stddev_rolling(..., 15/30)` rows. Confirm this is intended for ideas like I2 whose seeds sit outside their own MUST set (seed #2 carries day_mean, which is not in grammar.day_ops) — otherwise the wrap will refuse a family the idea actually wanted, and the right change is to widen MUST for that idea rather than to keep the bypass.

5. The two affected rows in episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold/evidence.json are pre-existing output of the buggy run; they scored -0.90 and -1.04 and did not change the "0 passers" verdict, so no re-run is required to protect a conclusion — but the episode note should record that the steer arm's MUST gate was not enforced on window/constant mutants of seeds.
